posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Etheria:

Yeah. I already spent most of the day crying… This came on an emotionally fragile day for me :( Interested about 'Daybreak' though - I am going to speculate that Ra2 is on the team, and maybe Visioary, because I like the idea ofher beiong friends with FP Legacy 

Daybreak seems like the new mentee team of the Sentinels of Freedom, and they said it consists of "all-new characters."  So my understanding is that it's going to be 5 characters we've never even seen hints of before, and my guess is that they're going to be the "archetype" characters for the RPG, i.e. pregenerated characters that players can either use as PC's as they are, or use them as a starting point for building their own.  If that's the case, I'm expecting them to represent the most common mechanical superhero archetypes:

  • Super-strength or FISS (flying/invulnerability/strength/speed)
  • Speedster
  • Blaster (energy attacks)
  • "Normal" (martial artist, guns, gadgets, etc.)
  • Mystic/psychic
  • Suit (Bunker, Benchmark, etc.)
I know that's 6, but I'm not confident enough to narrow it down to 5.  And I know mystic and psychic aren't really the same, but you don't usually see both at once.  There are lots of other superhero archetypes, but they're less common and more niche.  Oh, and I'm betting exactly one will be nonhuman, probably an alien.

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Arcanist Lupus:

My understanding was that it was four new characters + Legacy.  Which checks off your first and third archetypes right there.  I'm skeptical that they'd include a new speedster unless that hero had something that clearly differentiated them from Tachyon, though.  Same goes for the suited hero, since the old FV had two of those.

I wasn't sure whether they were counting Felicia, but they did say "all new heroes."  Although it's also not 100% clear that Daybreak and the default hero team are one and the same.

If Felicia is part of the team, though, she's a FISS through-and-through.  FISSes frequently have oddball powers thrown into their mix, but like her laser eyes, they're typically single-purpose.  True Blasters, like Ra and Tempest, are more versatile with their attack powers, being able to shape and control the energies they unleash in a wide range of different ways for different purposes.  The Atomic Glare seems to be purely a point-and-shoot deal.

Good thought on Daybreak being former Citizens of the Sun.  It would make perfect sense for a junior powered team suddenly coming from nowhere and working together right off the bat, and of course "breaking away from the Sun" is a perfect description.
